newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down one to 838 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down one to 838 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 838 as of November 8, down one from the prior week and 69 above the year-ago total of 769, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by three to 706, while rigs working offshore rose one to 105. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose one to 27.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in California, which showed an increase of five and Oklahoma, which showed a decrease of four. Texas rose by three and Louisiana fell by four.

A total of 349 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up three from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by five to 486, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects dropped by 11 to three.
There were 195 rigs drilling directionally, 70 drilling horizontally and 573 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by one to 311 versus 204 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
